Grouping the two middle calls to the right gives 2, a counter that jumps by two reports 8, and turning the subtraction into an addition gives 11.
questions.hint: Count the calls, then apply the arithmetic in the order the operators bind.
questions.learningObjective: trace the call order and the value of an expression with four calls

3:4, because all four calls run and the product binds tighter

options.misconception: believes the two middle calls group to the right of the plus
options.text: 2:4, because the two middle calls group to the right of the plus

options.misconception: believes the counter advances by two for every call it receives
options.text: 3:8, because the counter advances by two for every call it receives

questions.topic: Order Of Evaluation Across A Whole Expression

questions.explanation: The throw leaves the inner try block, the inner finally clause runs on the way out, and the exception then reaches the outer catch clause, after which the outer finally clause runs, giving abcd in that order. Removing any one of the three clauses removes exactly its own letter, which is what the three wrong readings do.
questions.hint: The exception is handled outside the inner try block, but inside the outer one.

questions.topic: Two Finally Clauses Around One Exception

questions.explanation: The return settles its value at the moment it runs, and the finally clause then adds a hundred to the cell that was being examined, so the caller receives 1 and reads 96 out of the row. A finally clause that changed nothing would leave minus four, a return one further along would report 2, and adding twice as much would leave 196.
questions.hint: The row and the returned value change at different moments.
questions.learningObjective: trace a return that is settled before a finally clause changes the row

questions.topic: AReturn Decided Before The Finally Clause

questions.explanation: The declared resources are closed as the block is left, before control reaches the catch clause, and they close in the reverse of the order they were opened, so the log reads openA, openB, body, closeB, closeA, catch. A catch clause that records nothing drops the last word, declaring the names the other way round swaps the whole log, and a body that records nothing drops the middle word.
questions.hint: The resources belong to the block, so they are released as the block is left.
questions.learningObjective: trace resources that close before an exception is handled

questions.topic: Resources Close Before The Catch Clause

questions.explanation: A finally clause that must leave the row alone still has to run, so the only change that reports the original cells is the one that stores each cell back into its own place. Adding a constant leaves 12 and 15, doubling leaves 4 and 10, and copying the first cell into each one leaves 2 and 2.

questions.topic: Breaks In Two Loops That Nest

questions.explanation: The first pass leaves the count at ten, the second pass raises it to twenty and then throws, the catch clause adds its one, and the third pass raises it to 31. A catch clause that adds nothing lets the third pass reach 30, a pass that added one would leave 4, and a fourth pass would carry the count to 41.
questions.hint: The throw happens after the addition on that pass, not before it.

questions.topic: The Value A Catch Clause Sees

questions.explanation: The first call returns false, and only a short circuiting and will leave the right hand side unevaluated, so the helper is asked once and the program prints false:1. A plain ampersand asks both calls and prints false:2, an exclusive or also asks both and prints true:2, and a bitwise and between a boolean and a number does not compile at all.
questions.hint: One of the two operators that evaluate both sides would report a call count of two.
questions.learningObjective: complete the condition that keeps the second guard from being asked
